Starter kit: Offing alongside Renovate and Dependabot

Most repositories already run an update bot. Renovate and Dependabot keep dependencies moving and open security updates; neither knows whether a package is deprecated, retired, or past its support window. Offing adds that lifecycle layer, and it prints configuration for both bots so their next pull requests start from the findings in this repository.

Both generators scan the repository offline and print to stdout. Neither edits a config file, and the scan makes no network requests.

What each tool reports

Renovate Dependabot Offing
Keeps dependencies current yes, from its config and schedule yes, weekly or daily per ecosystem and directory no; it reports, it does not update
Security updates yes yes names affected versions and, where bundled data has them, advisory ids
Lifecycle status only what its config tells it no deprecated, end-of-support, end-of-life, removed, or scheduled, per rule
Evidence release notes it can read changelog links it finds rule id, authoritative source URL, deadline, severity, exact location
Replacement applies a replacementName you configure no names the replacement in the finding, and offing context builds migration steps
Runtime pins allowedVersions you configure no equivalent Node.js and Python end-of-life findings

The bots decide when to change a version. Offing decides whether the current one is still supported and what to say about it. Run them together rather than choosing one.

Sample repository

The outputs below come from a small sample repository:

{
  "name": "update-bots-sample",
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": { "request": "^2.88.2", "node-sass": "^9.0.0" },
  "engines": { "node": ">=18" }
}

with 18 in .nvmrc and actions/checkout@v2 in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Both commands were run from that directory; the results are deterministic, so the same repository always prints the same fragments.

Generate both fragments

From the repository root:

npx @velella/offing renovate-preset . > renovate-fragment.json
npx @velella/offing dependabot-config . > dependabot-fragment.yml

Renovate fragment

{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "description": "Generated by Offing from repository lifecycle findings. Review before merging into renovate.json; Offing does not edit config files.",
  "packageRules": [
    {
      "description": "Offing: keep Node.js on a supported release (nodejs.runtime.eol-18)",
      "matchDatasources": ["node-version"],
      "matchPackageNames": ["node"],
      "allowedVersions": ">=22"
    },
    {
      "description": "Offing: replace node-sass (npm.package.node-sass.eol)",
      "matchDatasources": ["npm"],
      "matchPackageNames": ["node-sass"],
      "replacementName": "sass"
    }
  ]
}
  • A finding whose replacement is itself a package name becomes a replacementName rule. Prose replacements, such as request's "Native fetch or a maintained HTTP client", are skipped because Renovate cannot apply them.
  • Node.js and Python runtime findings become allowedVersions pins, so Renovate stays on a supported line instead of offering the next unsupported one.

Dependabot fragment

# Generated by Offing from repository lifecycle findings.
# Review before merging into .github/dependabot.yml; Offing does not edit files.
version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    groups:
      offing-deprecated-packages:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns:
          - "actions/checkout"
  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    groups:
      offing-deprecated-packages:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns:
          - "node-sass"
          - "request"
  • Each ecosystem and directory with findings gets a weekly entry whose groups.patterns list the affected packages, so their updates arrive in one reviewable pull request per directory instead of several.
  • Workflow findings always point at /, where Dependabot looks for .github/workflows itself. Runtime findings have no Dependabot equivalent and are skipped.
  • An empty scan prints comments only, never updates: [], which Dependabot rejects.

Set up Renovate

Merge the printed packageRules into the packageRules array in renovate.json and keep the rest of your config:

{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["config:recommended"],
  "packageRules": [
    {
      "description": "Offing: replace node-sass (npm.package.node-sass.eol)",
      "matchDatasources": ["npm"],
      "matchPackageNames": ["node-sass"],
      "replacementName": "sass"
    }
  ]
}

Validate before committing:

npx --yes --package renovate -- renovate-config-validator renovate.json

Renovate now retargets node-sass updates to sass and keeps the node-version datasource on 22 or later. It still decides when to open the pull request and how to group it. More detail: Feeding Renovate.

Set up Dependabot

Merge the printed updates entries into .github/dependabot.yml. Keep any entries you already have; do not duplicate an ecosystem and directory that is already listed.

version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    groups:
      offing-deprecated-packages:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns:
          - "node-sass"
          - "request"

The grouping is the point: Dependabot already updates those packages, and the group makes the deprecated ones land together so the migration is reviewed as one change. Dependabot does not replace node-sass with sass and has no runtime pin; those two parts come from Offing's findings and the Renovate fragment. More detail: Feeding Dependabot.

Keep the lifecycle gate in CI

Config fragments tell the bots what to do after a finding exists. The CI gate is what notices new findings, including usage that a bot pull request introduces. Copy the workflow from the Next.js starter:

- uses: velella-sh/offing@v0.7.1
  with:
    baseline: .offing-baseline.json
    fail-on-severity: high

Accepted findings go in the baseline, new ones fail the pull request, and the failure names the rule, source, deadline, and file. See GITHUB_ACTION.md for inputs and SARIF upload.

Keep the fragments current

The fragments are a snapshot of one scan. Regenerate them after a migration lands or dependency policy changes, review the diff, and delete rules that no longer apply:

npx @velella/offing renovate-preset . > renovate-fragment.json
npx @velella/offing dependabot-config . > dependabot-fragment.yml

Because the output is deterministic, a diff shows exactly which findings appeared or disappeared. Commit only the rules you merge into the real config; the generated files themselves can stay out of the repository.

What Offing does not do

The scan reads repository files and bundled lifecycle data only. It never evaluates repository code, never uses the network, never edits bot configuration, and never runs a migration command; it prints suggestions, and the verification commands in a migration packet are for a person or agent to run deliberately. Rules and their sources are reviewed data; see Lifecycle rules.
